summary.headline: RITES Q1 FY27 revenue grew 9-10% YoY, PAT about 8%; order book at INR 9,450 crore, with export revenue slipping into Q2 on Bangladesh first rake.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as growth of 9-10% YoY in revenue and about 8% at the bottom line, driven by the record order book from last year, but said execution must step up sequentially. Export revenue from the Bangladesh coach order was not recognised in Q1 because the first rake (about 20 coaches, four coach types) was still being finalised; dispatch is expected within about 10 days, with recognition in Q2. Consolidated EBITDA margin was 22% and PAT margin about 17%, both held sequentially, and management reiterated red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT margin. Order book reached INR 9,450 crore after 128 fresh orders worth INR 670 crore, with about 70% of fresh orders won competitively.

financial_highlights.change: Strike rate about 1.4 orders a day
Expected to grow at least double digit in FY27
Dividend to RITES about INR 10 crore, about 91% payout

segments.name: Export (rolling stock and locomotives)
segments.commentary: Export order book about INR 1,775 crore, of which about INR 900 crore is Bangladesh (200 coaches, about 10 rakes); balance is locomotives including Mozambique and African countries. Management targets at least INR 300 crore export revenue in FY27 and about 15% of total revenue.

segments.name: International project consultancy (RITES Videsh)
segments.commentary: Combined export and foreign consultancy order book INR 2,100 crore as of 30 June 2026. Management expects current book to largely execute by next FY.

segments.name: Turnkey projects
segments.commentary: About 50% of order book (about INR 4,700 crore of INR 9,450 crore) and about 30-33% of Q1 revenue; margins about 1.5-2%.

segments.name: Consultancy (domestic PMC/project)
segments.commentary: Balance of order book (about INR 4,700 crore) split roughly 50-50 with export rolling stock consultancy; majority of fresh consultancy wins on competitive basis, with tougher margins.

segments.name: REMCL (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Profit about INR 22 crore in Q1 with about 50%+ PAT margin; early progress in international and domestic renewable consultancy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided as substantial vs FY26; management aims for double-digit revenue growth and sequential increase in quarterly revenue.
Export revenue target of at least INR 300 crore in FY27; visibility on Mozambique deliveries and Bangladesh rake cadence expected by end-Q2.
Bangladesh 200-coach order: management expects completion in early Q2 or Q3 of FY28, not this year.
Mozambique locomotive deliveries targeted to begin by end of FY27, with clearer visibility by end-Q2.
Red lines: consolidated EBITDA margin at least 20% and PAT margin at least 15% on an annual basis; quarterly fluctuation possible.
FY28 employee cost growth guided at about 8-10%, not 20%, driven by pay revision and headcount.
capex_capacity: Bangladesh coach production in mass production after prototype approval; first rake of about 20 coaches to ship within about 10 days of the call.
Subsequent rakes expected to take less time as designs are approved.
Low capex and minimal working capital needs cited; company described as debt free.
Headcount rose to about 3,125 from about 2,675 YoY to build bench strength; pipeline of 200+ further hires tied to new inflows.
Vande Bharat on standard gauge: prototype development and talks with Indian Railways at an early stage; export interest from some countries.
demand_pricing: Order inflow of 128 orders worth INR 670 crore in Q1; about 70% of fresh orders won through competitive bidding.

Export orders are mostly global competitive tenders; management targets one export order per quarter. About 35 million (USD or currency unspecified) order for nine locomotives from South Africa announced in July, not yet in order book pending agreement signing.
Management says margins on competitively won orders are tighter; mitigation is prioritising higher-margin orders in each quarter or half year.
Travel costs under pressure in consultancy; guardrails in place.
Turnkey share expected to average below 50% over time, though clients prefer single-point turnkey contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Bangladesh export revenue not recognised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised per full rake; first rake of about 20 coaches (four types) had final approval delayed by a few days, and dispatch is expected within about 10 days, so recognition falls in Q2. Later rakes should be faster.

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of pending export orders and timelines for Bangladesh and Mozambique?
qa_highlights.answer: Export order book about INR 1,775 crore, with about INR 900 crore Bangladesh; Bangladesh will not finish this year, likely early Q2 or Q3 FY28. Mozambique deliveries may start by end-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much export revenue this year and next?
qa_highlights.answer: At least INR 300 crore export revenue in FY27; export targeted at about 15% of total revenue this year, with the current order book largely executed next FY.

qa_highlights.question: Turnkey margins and order book accounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Turnkey is about 50% of order book with margins of about 1.5-2%; full contract value (for example INR 105 crore vs INR 5 crore fee) is booked in order book and revenue flows through P&L.

qa_highlights.question: Margin outlook: has margin bottomed?
qa_highlights.answer: Pressure from competitive pricing, turnkey mix, travel costs and upcoming pay revision; EBITDA held at 22% and PAT at about 17%, with red lines of 20% EBITDA and 15% PAT on an annual basis.

qa_highlights.question: FY28 employee cost increase and turnkey share outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY28 employee cost growth of about 8-10%, not 20%; turnkey expected to average below 50% over time, though clients favour turnkey.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy and REMCL outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Payout expected to stay at 90%+ with no major business model change; REMCL profit about INR 22 crore with about INR 10 crore dividend to RITES, and early progress in renewables.

risks_watch: Export revenue timing: Bangladesh rake cadence and Mozambique delivery start depend on execution and clarity by end-Q2.
Margin pressure from competitive wins, rising turnkey mix, travel costs and FY28 pay revision; watch EBITDA vs 20% red line.
Mozambique and South Africa orders: South Africa 9-locomotive order not yet in order book pending formal agreement.
Employee cost rise (about 450 added YoY) must be matched by revenue execution.
QA revenue steady at about INR 70 crore; FY27 target of double-digit growth.
key_quotes: We need to really step on the gas and keep on improving the execution sequentially over the coming quarters, so that the entire FY is as per the guidance

Our red lines of 20% EBITDA margins and 15% PAT margin on a consol basis, we will definitely strategically pushing on the execution of some higher margin orders out of the 700 plus order that we are executing.
Not really 20%. I would put it more in the range of about 8-10%.
We are not really a very keen on taking much on Turnkey basis.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on the order book and roadmap, but explicitly cautious on sequential execution, margins and export timing. Management was evasive on Mozambique start timing and Bangladesh rake cadence, deferring firm visibility to end-Q2.
